ASPCA lists avermectins (ivermectin, selamectin, moxidectin) as the #2 toxic cause of tremors in cats, but gives no explicit topical-toxicity statement for cats.

effect: Drooling, vomiting, ataxia, tremors, seizures, hypoglycemia, liver/kidney failure.

sources.title: Pet Poison Helpline: Camphor

notes: Extra candidate. PPH: "Camphor is readily absorbed across the skin, and should never be applied to dogs or cats due to risks for poisoning." Found in Vicks VapoRub, Tiger Balm, Campho-Phenique, Carmex, arthritis rubs.

ingredient: cationic surfactants / quaternary ammonium (benzalkonium chloride, cetrimonium bromide)
effect: Oral/esophageal/gastric burns, hemorrhagic gastritis, drooling, CNS depression; dermal burns or irritation and corneal ulcers with concentrated products.

Pet Poison Helpline: Liquid Potpourri

notes: Extra candidate. ASPCApro: ingestion "can be more serious, particularly in cats who appear to be sensitive to these surfactants"; "dermal burns may occur with dermal exposure of concentrated products." Liquid potpourri (cationic detergents and essential oils) is among the top-10 feline toxicoses, with cats licking it off fur. No threshold given. These ingredients appear in some shampoos/conditioners; the sources discuss cleaners and potpourri.

safe_exceptions: PPH: "Single or sporadic ingestion by pets of low concentration propylene glycol as found in cosmetics or prepared foods is generally recognized as safe."
effect: Cats: repeated ingestion causes severe anemia; high-concentration (antifreeze) ingestion causes neurologic signs.

threshold: PPH: "Neurologic signs seen with exposures to concentrated products (>40%) include tremors, seizures, coma, and death."
safe_exceptions: ASPCA: fipronil "is safe for most mammals when used properly"; rabbits are the sensitive species.
effect: Ingestion: salivation, vomiting; application-site irritation/alopecia.
